newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senators introduce CPI resolution.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senators introduce CPI resolution.

text.p: The Senate Finance Committee's chairman and ranking Democrat Wednesday introduced a resolution aimed at testing for support to make the Consumer Price Index more accurate.

The non-binding resolution from committee Chairman William Roth, a Republican from Delaware, and Sen. Daniel Patrick Moynihan, a New York Democrat, stated "all cost of living adjustments required by statute should accurately reflect the best available estimate of changes in the cost of living."
An advisory commission reported in December that the CPI overstated the cost of living by 1.1 percentage points.

"Inaccurate government statistics -- particularly one as important as the CPI -- are unacceptable," Roth said. "Steps should be taken to change the procedures so that the measure of inflation is as accurate as possible," he said.
The issue must be addressed in a bipartisan manner with the White House taking the lead, Roth said in a statement.
"To do nothing in the face of overwhelming evidence would be a political decision; wrong-headed and short-sighted, with large long-term implications," Moynihan said.

The resolution was the first step in trying to see if there was support for the issue, a committee spokeswoman said. If enough support appears, there would be a possibility of drafting legislation instructing the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics to make the CPI more accurate, she said.
